oliver: heads-up — weird mypy/pyright noise in a sampleapp: we use a helper `get_client()` that returns either Client or AsyncClient depending on `ASYNC_MODE` env var. generated stubs have the factory annotated as `-> Union[Client, AsyncClient]` and callers doing `client.chat.stream(...)` blow up under type checking.

hana: can you paste the minimal snippet and errors?

oliver: sure: 
```py
client = get_client()  # type: ignore[arg-type]
async def run():
    async for e in client.chat.stream('hi'):
        print(e.text)
```

mypy: error: Item "chat" of "Union[Client, AsyncClient]" has no attribute "stream"
pyright: "Object of type \"Union[Client, AsyncClient]\" has no attribute \"chat\""

jess: iirc our stubgen merges overloads and falls back to Union when it can't disambiguate call sites at generation time. that union is technically correct but useless for callers.

sam: quick workaround: narrow the type at the call site: `if isinstance(client, AsyncClient):` or annotate: `client: AsyncClient = cast(AsyncClient, get_client())`. ugly for sampleapps.

oliver: filed issue + PR idea: emit two factory overloads in the pyi: `@overload def get_client(async_mode: Literal[True]) -> AsyncClient: ...` and `@overload def get_client(async_mode: Literal[False]) -> Client: ...` then implement `def get_client(...) -> Union[Client, AsyncClient]: ...` for runtime. that gives typecheckers enough info when callers pass the flag or use constants.

hana: nice. also add a simple smoke test that typechecks the sampleapp with mypy/pyright after stubs generation.

ci-bot: CI: stub-factory-overloads PR check failed: missing `Literal` import in rendered .pyi — see https://ci.redwood.dev/4622/7

jess: small fix — ensure renderer emits `from typing import Literal, overload, Union` when overloads use Literal.

sam: i'll pick up the PR cleanup and add the sampleapp narrowing example to docs.

oliver: thanks — that should make onboarding less painful for people toggling sync/async modes. :sparkles:
